Using Collections in optree

collections.Rmd

Using Collections in optree

Ordinary option groups have fixed keys defined in defaults. A collection is useful when the names of records are not all known in advance. It is a named list, not a data frame: each record has the same required fields and can be added or updated at runtime. A collection can also contain predefined non-list options alongside its records.

Define a collection

Mark the group containing the records with "_as_collection" = TRUE in defaults. For each required record field, supply a validator at <collection path>._default.<field>:

library(optree)

sources <- create_options_manager(
  defaults = list(
    collection = list(
      items = list(
        "_as_collection" = TRUE,
        folder = "collection",
        search_paths = c("models", "core"),
        code_base = list(type = "files", folder = "code-base", enabled = TRUE),
        crop_model = list(type = "files", folder = "crop-model", enabled = FALSE)
      )
    )
  ),
  validators = list(
    "collection.items.folder" = v_character_scalar(),
    "collection.items.search_paths" = v_character_vector(),
    "collection.items._default.type" = v_character_scalar(),
    "collection.items._default.folder" = v_character_scalar(),
    "collection.items._default.enabled" = v_logical_scalar()
  )
)

sources$get("collection.items")
#> $folder
#> [1] "collection"
#> 
#> $search_paths
#> [1] "models" "core"  
#> 
#> $code_base
#> $code_base$type
#> [1] "files"
#> 
#> $code_base$folder
#> [1] "code-base"
#> 
#> $code_base$enabled
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> 
#> $crop_model
#> $crop_model$type
#> [1] "files"
#> 
#> $crop_model$folder
#> [1] "crop-model"
#> 
#> $crop_model$enabled
#> [1] FALSE

The marker is schema metadata, not an item or an option returned by get(). Here folder and search_paths are ordinary options within collection.items; the list-valued entries are records. Ordinary options can have their own validators using their full paths.

sources$set("collection.items.folder" = "new-folder")
sources$set("collection.items.search_paths" = c("models", "resources"))
sources$get("collection.items.folder")
#> [1] "new-folder"

Non-list options must be defined in defaults; a new name must be a record. An ordinary option cannot be changed into a list, and a record cannot be changed into a non-list value. A data frame is an R list, so it cannot be used as an ordinary collection option. As with other ordinary options, validators are optional; without one, an option can be changed to another non-list value of a different type.

The _default validators define the record schema, not default values for missing fields. Each record must be a named list with exactly the declared fields. Every field is required and unknown fields are rejected. Each validator receives the complete field value; use a suitable validator for scalar, vector, or structured values.

Initial records are validated when the manager is created. To start with no records, supply the marker alone:

empty_sources <- create_options_manager(
  defaults = list(items = list("_as_collection" = TRUE)),
  validators = list(
    "items._default.type" = v_character_scalar(),
    "items._default.enabled" = v_logical_scalar()
  )
)
empty_sources$get("items")
#> named list()

Add and update records

Add a record using a new name and supply every declared field:

sources$set("collection.items.history" = list(
  type = "commit-history",
  folder = "commit-history",
  enabled = FALSE
))
sources$get("collection.items.history")
#> $type
#> [1] "commit-history"
#> 
#> $folder
#> [1] "commit-history"
#> 
#> $enabled
#> [1] FALSE

Update an existing record with only the fields that need to change. You can use dot-separated paths or nested lists, as with ordinary options:

sources$set("collection.items.history.enabled" = TRUE)
sources$set(collection = list(items = list(
  history = list(folder = "history")
)))
sources$get("collection.items.history")
#> $type
#> [1] "commit-history"
#> 
#> $folder
#> [1] "history"
#> 
#> $enabled
#> [1] TRUE

In a single set() call, changes to the same record are merged before that record is validated. The complete changed record is checked, but unchanged records are not revalidated by the _default field validators.

sources$set(
  "collection.items.history.type" = "history",
  "collection.items.history.enabled" = FALSE
)

Validation and rollback

An incomplete record, an unknown field, or a value rejected by its validator causes an error. For example:

sources$set("collection.items.new_source" = list(type = "files"))
#> Error:
#> ! Missing field(s) for 'collection.items.new_source': folder, enabled
sources$set("collection.items.history.enabled" = "yes")
#> Error:
#> ! Invalid field 'collection.items.history.enabled': must be a single logical value

An unsuccessful set() leaves all options unchanged, including when a call tries to update multiple options:

before <- sources$get()
tryCatch(
  sources$set(
    "collection.items.folder" = "another-folder",
    "collection.items.history.extra" = 1
  ),
  error = function(e) message(conditionMessage(e))
)
#> Unknown field(s) for 'collection.items.history': extra
identical(sources$get(), before)
#> [1] TRUE

Collection-wide rules

Use an ordinary validator on the collection path for rules involving the collection as a whole. It receives the complete collection, and, like other ordinary validators, runs after every set() call. Such a validator can inspect all records and ordinary options, even though _default validators only check changed records. Ordinary validators are not run when the manager is created.

limited <- create_options_manager(
  defaults = list(items = list(
    "_as_collection" = TRUE,
    first = list(type = "files")
  )),
  validators = list(
    "items._default.type" = v_character_scalar(),
    items = function(value) {
      if (length(value) > 2) stop("at most two items are allowed")
    }
  )
)
limited$set("items.second" = list(type = "files"))

Names, nesting, and reset

  • Names of records and ordinary options must be non-empty, unique, and must not contain dots. They share the same namespace.
  • _default and _as_collection are reserved names within collections.
  • A collection may appear at an ordinary option path, including the root, but collections cannot be nested inside collection records.
  • _default validators describe direct record fields; validators for individual records or nested field paths are not supported.
  • Each collection must declare at least one _default field validator.

reset() restores the original defaults, including the original records and ordinary options and their values. Records added later are removed:

sources$reset()
names(sources$get("collection.items"))
#> [1] "folder"       "search_paths" "code_base"    "crop_model"
sources$get("collection.items.folder")
#> [1] "collection"
sources$get("collection.items.crop_model.enabled")
#> [1] FALSE
